long_biography.plain_text:
From the courts of El Palmar, Carlos Alcaraz developed a game built on explosive movement, varied shots and frequent advances to the net. His father, a tennis coach and club administrator, gave him early instruction, while a local confectionery company helped pay for junior travel that his family could not afford. Former world No. 1 Juan Carlos Ferrero later coached him at his academy in Villena.

Alcaraz's first major victory at the US Open carried him to the top of the men's rankings while still a teenager. He went on to win on clay, grass and hard courts, completing a career sweep of the four majors at the 2026 Australian Open. He also represented Spain at the Paris Olympics, winning the men's singles silver medal.

proposed_details.existing_value:
Carlos Alcaraz (born 5 May 2003) is a Spanish professional tennis player and former world No. 1 in men’s singles. He finished as year-end No. 1 in 2022 and 2025, and has won 26 ATP singles titles, including seven Grand Slams and eight Masters titles. He is the youngest man to complete a Career Grand Slam.

Alcaraz turned professional in 2018 and broke into the top 100 in 2021, reaching the US Open quarterfinals that year. In 2022, he won his first major at the US Open and became the youngest world No. 1 in ATP history at age 19.

He won Wimbledon in 2023, defeating Novak Djokovic, and in 2024 became the youngest man in the Open Era to win both the French Open and Wimbledon in the same season. In 2025, he added French Open and US Open titles, and in 2026 won the Australian Open to complete the Career Grand Slam at age 22.
